periods.analysis: We are starting this cycle with the objective in red because the highest-risk district vehicle burglary rate is 15.8 per 1,000 against a target of <= 12, even as investigative follow-through is performing: case clearance is 57.2%, above the >= 55% standard. Mail, porch, and package theft reports sit at 20.1 per 1,000 households, above the <= 15 target and correctly marked yellow because the pattern is concentrated rather than citywide. The concentration is clearest along the West Harbor garage loop, Pier 6 visitor lots, and the airport employee-park-and-ride edges, where unlocked vehicles, rental plates, and late-night shift changes are creating repeat opportunity. Our posture is concerned but managed: the clearance result shows detectives and patrol are closing cases, but prevention in the target geography is not yet reducing exposure.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Auto Burglary Detail on the West Harbor Route A/B overnight grid and add two marked pass-throughs at Pier 6 and Bayfront Garage between 2200 and 0300. Sustain the green clearance performance by preserving the 48-hour detective triage standard and continuing evidence pickup from garages with camera IDs WHG-12 through WHG-19. For package theft, launch a focused carrier-and-building manager protocol in the Seaview, Old Port, and Midtown high-rise clusters, with weekly review of repeat addresses.

periods.analysis: The objective remains red in 2024-Q4 because the vehicle burglary rate in the highest-risk district moved the wrong direction, from 15.8 to 16 per 1,000, still well above the <= 12 target. Clearance improved from 57.2% to 59.2%, and that green movement matters because it reflects better case packaging by the Night Investigations pod and faster video retrieval from private garages. Mail, porch, and package theft reports also worsened from 20.1 to 21.9 per 1,000 households, a seasonal increase we expected around holiday deliveries but did not sufficiently blunt. The operating picture is mixed: our investigative process is disciplined, but visible prevention and repeat-location control are not yet strong enough.
periods.recommendations: Extend holiday package-theft suppression two weeks past the retail peak, not ending it on December 31, and assign Community Service Officers to the top 25 delivery rooms identified by CAD tags PKG-04 and PKG-07. Maintain the case-clearance gains by keeping the detective intake checklist mandatory for vehicle burglary series and using the Digital Evidence Portal for all garage-camera uploads within one business day. For the red vehicle-burglary measure, shift one traffic-safety overtime car to West Harbor lots on Thursday through Sunday nights until the rate is below 15 per 1,000 for two consecutive monthly reads.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q1 the red condition persists, with the highest-risk district vehicle burglary rate rising again from 16 to 16.2 per 1,000 against the <= 12 target. Case clearance improved from 59.2% to 60.1%, the best point in this sequence so far and still safely green over the >= 55% standard. Package theft eased from 21.9 to 20.5 per 1,000 households, but it remains yellow and well above the <= 15 target, particularly in buildings with unsecured lobby shelving. The procedural concern is that we are solving a larger share of cases while the same environmental opportunities continue to generate new ones.
periods.recommendations: Hold the clearance model steady: keep the Q1 detective-screening cohort intact, continue same-day pawn and online marketplace checks, and audit five closed cases per week for victim notification quality. Stand up a 60-day Auto Entry Prevention Sprint focused on the airport hotel corridor, Bayfront Garage, and Pier 6, with license-plate reader alerts reviewed by a supervisor before deployment to protect community trust. Require property managers in the top 15 package-theft buildings to adopt locked delivery rooms or scheduled carrier handoff windows before the next quarterly review.

periods.analysis: The objective is still red in 2025-Q2, but there is modest stabilization: vehicle burglary moved from 16.2 down to 16.1 per 1,000, still far above the <= 12 target. Clearance slipped from 60.1% to 59.5%, but it remains green and above the >= 55% threshold, so the investigative pipeline is holding. Package theft improved materially from 20.5 to 18.2 per 1,000 households after the carrier handoff work and building-manager contacts, though the measure remains yellow. This quarter shows that procedural fixes can move the theft environment, but the auto burglary problem is not yet responding at the scale required.
periods.recommendations: Continue the package-theft playbook in the same buildings and extend it to the next 20 addresses before summer travel volume increases. For vehicle burglary, convert the 60-day sprint into a CompStat standing item with beat-level ownership for West Harbor Route A/B, the airport hotel corridor, and the Pier 6 surface lots. Preserve the green clearance result by backfilling summer leave in Property Crimes with two trained light-duty officers assigned to report review and video requests.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q3 the overall status remains red because vehicle burglary worsened from 16.1 to 16.3 per 1,000 in the highest-risk district, moving away from the <= 12 target. Case clearance declined from 59.5% to 58.2%, still green above >= 55%, but the downward movement deserves attention before it becomes a capacity issue. Package theft also increased from 18.2 to 19.9 per 1,000 households, consistent with summer tourism, student move-ins near Midtown, and more short-term rental turnover. The pattern tells us our spring controls were real but not durable enough through seasonal pressure.
periods.recommendations: Add a September surge plan for move-in corridors: two evening foot teams in Midtown, one plain-clothes package-theft team at the Seaview parcel lockers, and directed patrol around short-term rental blocks with repeat reports. Require the Auto Burglary Detail to produce a weekly prevention memo naming the top five lots, the lighting or access-control defect, and the accountable property contact. To protect clearance, set a 72-hour supervisory review trigger for any vehicle burglary case with video available but not yet requested.

periods.analysis: The red condition deepens in 2025-Q4: vehicle burglary increased from 16.3 to 16.4 per 1,000, and the measure remains substantially above the <= 12 target. Clearance recovered from 58.2% to 59.6%, which is green and shows that the supervisory review trigger helped restore investigative discipline. Package theft climbed from 19.9 to 21.5 per 1,000 households, another holiday-season rise and still yellow against the <= 15 target. We are managing the work, but the public will judge us by fewer break-ins and fewer stolen deliveries, not only by better case closure.
periods.recommendations: Keep the 72-hour supervisory review trigger because it helped move clearance back to 59.6%, and make it permanent for all property-crime series cases. For holiday package theft, deploy Operation Doorstep Shield at the 30 highest-report buildings, pairing carrier time-window agreements with lobby signage, decoy parcel operations, and victim follow-up within two business days. For vehicle burglary, require written prevention agreements with the owners of Bayfront Garage, HarborPoint Lot C, and the airport hotel lots, including lighting repairs, camera-angle corrections, and overnight attendant logs.

periods.analysis: The objective remains red in 2026-Q1 because the vehicle burglary rate rose again from 16.4 to 16.5 per 1,000, with no progress toward the <= 12 target. Clearance improved from 59.6% to 60%, remaining green and confirming that the detective process is reliable when evidence is captured early. Package theft improved from 21.5 to 20 per 1,000 households after the holiday peak, but it remains yellow and above the <= 15 target. The operational gap is now clear: investigation is functioning, while place-based prevention in the highest-risk district still lacks enough compliance from private lots and buildings.
periods.recommendations: Escalate noncompliant private parking facilities to a joint Police-Code Enforcement review, starting with HarborPoint Lot C and the airport hotel cluster, and document lighting, camera, and access-control deficiencies by asset location. Sustain clearance by retaining the property-crime evidence liaison and adding a monthly quality check on victim contact, suspect identification, and prosecutable-case submission. For package theft, keep Operation Doorstep Shield in the 30-building cohort and add parcel-locker vendor meetings with SecureBox and PortDrop to address overflow practices.

periods.analysis: In 2026-Q2 the objective is still red: the vehicle burglary rate held flat at 16.5 per 1,000 from last quarter, remaining well above the <= 12 target. Case clearance moved down from 60% to 59.1%, still green against the >= 55% standard, but the decline is a watch item as summer call volume approaches. Package theft improved from 20 to 18.4 per 1,000 households, continuing the post-holiday reduction but still yellow and not yet at the <= 15 target. The chronological arc is consistent: Harborview is clearing cases at a trustworthy rate, yet the highest-risk district remains the unresolved pressure point requiring tighter prevention, owner accountability, and measured enforcement.
periods.recommendations: Set a Q3 operating requirement that the highest-risk district produce a reduction plan for each of the top 10 vehicle-burglary micro-locations, with owner commitments, patrol dosage, and a monthly result review. Maintain the green clearance foundation by protecting detective staffing through summer leave and using retired-annuitant evidence technicians for video collection where permissible. Extend the package-theft building cohort from 30 to 45 sites, but only where managers agree to locked delivery storage, carrier scans at point of handoff, and monthly incident reconciliation with the department.

periods.analysis: Clearance remains above target and both theft rates improved, but vehicle burglary in the highest-risk district is still 16.2 per 1,000 against a ceiling of 12.0. The objective remains below plan despite movement in the right direction.
periods.recommendations: Concentrate place-management and repeat-offender reviews at the highest-volume parking locations while protecting investigative follow-up time.
